articles.title: Trump: FBI utreder Nvidia-chefen
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Trump: FBI utreder Nvidia-chefen
articles.body_text: Jensen Huang tar emot en utmärkelse av Donald Trump i samband med ett evenemang i Washington den 8 oktober. Nvidias vd Jensen Huang utreds av FBI. Det säger USA:s president Donald Trump sedan Huang erkänt att han haft en affär med en spionanklagad kvinna. Jag vet att FBI tittar på det, säger Trump vid en pressträff i Vita huset på måndagen. Presidenten tillägger att han pratat med Huang som han tror ”kommer att klara sig bra”. Han beskriver också chipmagnaten som ”en hederlig man”. Nvidia meddelade under söndagskvällen att man inlett en utredning av vd:n Jensen Huang till följd av otrohetsaffären med Alice Huang, som amerikansk säkerhetstjänst enligt flera medier anser är en kinesisk spion

articles.title: AI-stjärnans spionanklagade älskarinna försvunnen
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: AI-stjärnans spionanklagade älskarinna försvunnen
articles.body_text: Jensen och Alice Huang vid en restaurang i Taipei maj 2025. AI-stjärnans spionanklagade älskarinna försvunnen Spionanklagade Alice Huang har genom sitt företag Megaspeed kommit över känslig information från den amerikanska AI-bjässen Nvidia. Hon har haft en otrohetsaffär med Nvidias toppchef och misstänks ha spionerat för Kinas räkning. Nu är det få som vet var hon befinner sig. Nvidias vd Jensen Huang har varit otrogen mot sin fru. Företagets styrelse ska utreda om han varit ett mål för en kinesisk spion. Men det finns inga skäl att tro att affärshemligheter eller USA:s nationella säkerhet har äventyrats, enligt ett pressmeddelande från techjätten. Uppgifterna är känsliga eftersom amerikanska tjänstemän i fjol kom fram till att hans älskarinna, Alice Huang, delat information med den kinesiska regeringen när hon jobbade med Nvidia för att bygga datacenter i Asien, enligt The Wall Street Journal s källor. Affärsidén var att bygga datahallar i sydöstra Asien med chip från Nvidia, och sedan hyra ut datakapacitet. Företaget blev efter ett par år en av Nvidias största kunder i regionen – och importerade chip för över 4,6 miljarder dollar, rapporterar Bloomberg . Men företaget misstänks ha smugglat vidare den viktiga tekniken till Kina, vilket är förbjudet. Megaspeed nekade till anklagelserna och uppgav för Bloomberg i fjol att man följer lagen, inklusive USA:s exportkontrollregler. Samtidigt som Megaspeeds chipleveranser rullade in, började Jensen och Alice Huang umgås. De drack whisky tillsammans med andra AI-chefer på en bar i Taipei i juni 2024 efter en konferens. Ett år senare åt de middag ihop med andra branschkollegor, och taiwanesiska medier filmade när Alice gav Jensen en kyss på kinden samtidigt som han intervjuades av journalister, skriver The New York Times . Amerikanska myndigheter har i över ett år utrett Alice Huangs företag Megaspeeds kopplingar till den kinesiska regeringen. Även Singapore och Taiwan har utrett hennes kopplingar till kinesisk underrättelseverksamhet och misstänker att hon blivit rekryterad efter att Peking insett hur nära hon stod Nvidia-toppen, skriver The Wall Street Journal . Alice Huang gick under jorden och försvann i Kina under en tid i slutet av 2024 i samband med att myndigheter började övervaka henne, skriver WSJ . Det är i dag svårt att fastställa var hon befinner sig och om hon fortfarande har en roll på Megaspeed. Flera internationella medier har utan framgång försökt nå henne för en kommentar. Under måndagen tillbakavisade en talesperson för den kinesiska regeringen uppgifterna om att Alice Huang skulle vara en spion.

articles.title: Pensionsavtal klart för över två miljoner svenskar
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Pensionsavtal klart för över två miljoner svenskar
articles.body_text: Efter långa förhandlingar har parterna nått en överenskommelse. Arkivbild. Pensionsavtal klart för över två miljoner svenskar Svenskt Näringsliv, LO och PTK har nått en överenskommelse om avtalspension, försäkring och omställning för över två miljoner privatanställda arbetare och tjänstemän. Från den 1 januari 2028 börjar inbetalningarna till tjänstepensionen ITP 1 vid 24 års ålder i stället för 25 och fortsätter sedan fram till 67 år i stället för 66, skriver PTK på sin sajt. Även den kollektivavtalade arbetsskadeförsäkringen TFA förändras, där självrisken och gränsen för minsta utbetalning tas bort. ”Samtidigt förbättras det kollektivavtalade föräldrapenningstilläget vid byte av arbetsgivare. Den innebär också förbättrade regler för att kvalificera sig för stöd från omställningsorganisationen. Förändringarna berör arbetare och tjänstemän som omfattas av Svenskt Näringslivs avtalsområden”, skriver organisationerna i ett gemensamt pressmeddelande. Berörda förbund och deras motparter ska nu anta överenskommelsen, processen blir klar först när berörda parter undertecknat avtalet.

articles.title: 350 000 SAS-kunder i misstänkt dataläcka
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: 350 000 SAS-kunder i misstänkt dataläcka
articles.body_text: Drygt 350 000 SAS-resenärers uppgifter kan ha blivit röjda. Arkivbild. 350 000 SAS-kunder i misstänkt dataläcka Hundratusentals SAS-resenärers bokningsuppgifter kan ha blivit röjda i en stor dataläcka, rapporterar SVT Nyheter . Även ett stort antal kunder hos finländska Finnair kan vara berörda. SAS har gjort en anmälan till Integritetsskyddsmyndigheten (IMY) om händelsen. Flygbolaget uppger i anmälan att läckan främst gäller äldre bokningar och genomförda resor. Det ska röra sig om bokningsreferenser, datum, uppgifter om antal passagerare och flygrelaterad information. Totalt berörs 350 164 personer av händelsen, enligt SAS. Bolaget har valt att inte informera de berörda resenärerna, men det beslutet kan ändras om fler uppgifter kommer fram. Läckan har skett i det globala bokningsverktyget Amadeus, som en rad flygbolag använder. ”SAS känner till den säkerhetsincident som Amadeus har rapporterat och har informerats om att viss bokningsinformation med koppling till SAS har påverkats”, skriver SAS i en kommentar till SVT. Flygbolaget skriver vidare att ”nödvändiga anmälningar till berörda tillsynsmyndigheter” har gjorts. Även Finnair berörs av det inträffade. I ett pressmeddelande skriver Finnair att omkring 116 000 av företagets flygreservationer kan vara berörda. I dataläckan förekommer inte bara Finnair utan även andra flygbolag. I fredags rapporterade NRK att obehöriga kan ha haft tillgång till uppgifterna i Amadeus bokningssystem i upp till tre år. Bland annat gällde det resenärer hos Norwegian.

articles.title: Nvidias aktie rasade efter spionmisstankarna
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Nvidias aktie rasade efter spionmisstankarna
articles.body_text: Nvidias aktie rasade efter spionmisstankarna En otrohetsaffär med spionmisstankar skakar om Nvidia. Aktien rasade på börsen i New York, medan andra teknikaktier, däribland AI-jättens konkurrenter, steg kraftigt. Nvidias styrelse meddelade på söndagen att man inlett en utredning kring vd:n och grundaren Jensen Huangs otrohetsaffär med en kvinna som pekats ut som en spion som agerat på uppdrag av Kina. När veckans börshandel inleddes kom prislappen. Aktien, den näst största i världen sett till börsvärde, föll 4,3 procent. Raset gick mot strömmen, Nasdaqs tekniktunga kompositindex pekade samtidigt på plus 2,2 procent. Chipbolagen AMD och Broadcom, konkurrenter till Nvidia, rusade 13,2 respektive 8,8 procent efter kraftiga nedgångar i förra veckan. Breda S&P 500 stängde upp 2,4 procent, Dow Jones industriindex ökade 2,2 procent. Oljepriset har fortsatt nedåt efter förra veckans kraftiga prisfall. Ett fat Nordsjöolja (Brent) kostar på måndagskvällen 92,79 dollar.

articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Hur fungerar den publicistiska grunden för nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik på TV4?
articles.body_text: Hur fungerar den publicistiska grunden för nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik på TV4? 9 januari 2024 ・ Uppdaterad: 15 augusti 2025 TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsbevakning ska vara i ögonhöjd med tittarna. Vi vill vara nära, personliga och inkluderande. För alla i hela Sverige. Vi ska vara trovärdiga och relevanta. Vi testar nya visuella former och utvecklar det rörliga berättandet. Vi är både snabba, och fördjupande. Vi ger plats för både humor och allvar. Vi påverkar och berör. Vi avslöjar maktmissbruk, och värnar pressfrihet och yttrandefrihet. Vi producerar Nyhetsmorgon, Nyhetsdagen, Efter fem och kvällsnyheter. Vi nyhetsrapporterar på tv4.se och fördjupar i kortdokumentärerna Nyheterna Story. Vår mångfaldigt prisbelönta redaktion Kalla Fakta granskar makt och missförhållanden. TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsbevakning sker ur ett riksperspektiv, med hela Sverige och världen som bevakningsområde. Vi har 17 rikskorrar på sex orter i Sverige. De finns i Luleå, Umeå, Östersund, Skövde, Göteborg och Malmö. Vi bevakar världen via utrikesreportrar, korrar och stringers. Vår journalistik vilar på respekt för alla människors lika värde, oavsett politisk åskådning, religion eller sexuell läggning. Det innebär att vi låter många röster komma till tals, även de som bär åsikter som inte nödvändigtvis delas av medarbetarna på redaktionen eller TV4. Men det kan också innebära att vi tar bort artikelkommentarer som kränker, eller till exempel avstår gäster i direktsändning där vi bedömer att risken är stor för missbruk av öppenheten. TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik är oberoende och obunden. Den står fri från politiska partier, organisationer, och näringsliv. Vi har ingen ledarsida eller politisk färg. Innehållet på våra plattformar bedöms och värderas av redaktörer, producenter och av ansvarig utgivare före publicering. Vi följer grundlagen och skyddar våra källor när de önskar anonymitet. Om vi refererar uppgifter från andra medier redovisar vi vilka medier eller andra informationskällor det handlar om. Annars berättar vi hur vi själva tagit reda på informationen, dock alltid med största respekt för källskydd.

articles.title: SVT Sport möter Graham Potter
articles.summary: I oktober 2025 tog engelsmannen Graham Potter över som förbundskapten för det svenska herrlandslaget i fotboll - efter att hans föregångare Jon Dahl Tomasson misslyckats med att ta Sverige direkt till fotbolls-VM. 50-årige Potter har ett förflutet som tränare för Premier League-klubbarna Brighton och Chelsea. Men för den svenska publiken är han kanske främst förknippad med sitt tränarjobb i Östersunds FK, som han tog från division 2 ända upp till allsvenskan. Så hur ska då Graham Potter vända den negativa trend som herrlandslaget befinner sig i? Har han vad som krävs för att Sverige ska ta sig till VM i sommar? Det och mycket annat frågade SVT Sports programledare André Pops honom.

articles.title: Bortglömda fiskar
articles.summary: Teatrar och konserthus lockar allt oftare med olika sidoevenemang. Teater Västernorrland har musikquiz, Folkoperan sänder poddar från sin foajé och på Göteborgsoperan kan man höra föredrag eller vara med och dansa. De uppsluppna tillställningarna, före och efter konserter och föreställningar, lockar också en ny sorts publik. En av Östersjöfestivalens mest omtalade programpunkter, förutom musiken i Berwaldhallen, har varit “Bortglömda fiskar” - en oväntad kulinarisk träff med Kålrotsakademin och provsmakning av “svensk sushi”. “Gensvaret från publiken är enormt. Man vill bli överraskad”, konstaterar Emma Nyberg, exekutiv producent på Berwaldhallen. Och på frågan om vad nors och näbbgädda har att göra i ett konserthus kommer det självklara svaret snabbt: “Att äta gott och att lyssna på klassisk musik hör ihop, båda skärper och öppnar våra sinnen.”

articles.title: På ett ögonblick
articles.summary: Arne Bivrins stora passion är fågelfotografi. Han kliver in i en sagovärld och tar bilder som får folk att häpna, av ögonblick som bara existerar där och då. Efter en stor tragedi där hela livet förändrades på några sekunder överlevde han med hjälp av fotografin. Under ett år följer vi Arne när han tar sig an sitt livs största fotoprojekt. Naturfilm producerad av Emil Sergel.

articles.title: Epstein associate who still runs model agency 'put me in danger' says abuse survivor
articles.summary: A woman says an agency boss sent her to photoshoots at the sex offender's Florida beach home.
articles.body_text: A woman raped by Jeffrey Epstein says the president of the model agency representing her put her in danger, when he sent her to two photoshoots at the convicted sex offender's Florida beach house. At the time, in 2009, Epstein was serving a jail sentence for sex offences against a minor but was allowed to work each day from his home. "My agency's job was to protect me, and they failed. In fact, they put me in danger. And for that, they should be held accountable," she tells the BBC World Service. Roza was 18 when she was first sent to Epstein's Palm Beach home by MC2 Model Management's US branch, having only arrived in the US from Uzbekistan about a month earlier. MC2's US president at the time, Jeff Fuller, now runs another US model agency called The Source Models. "My agency knew exactly where I was. So Jeff knew exactly where I was going," says Roza. She shows us an expense statement suggesting Fuller himself booked her flight home from Palm Beach, following her second shoot at Epstein's home. Fuller has previously claimed he did not know Roza was going to Epstein's house. She says the photoshoots led to her being employed as an assistant to Epstein. Other survivors have explained how the financier used the recruitment of assistants as an elaborate ruse to allow him to continue abusing young women . Roza says Epstein went on to systematically rape her. Fuller has not responded to the BBC's allegations. He has previously said he did not know Roza was being abused. We discovered through the Epstein-related documents released by the US Department of Justice [DOJ] that 10 models from MC2 met, or were in communication with, Epstein after his conviction. The files also show Epstein gave $1m (£742,000) to MC2 in 2005 - despite the agency owners telling a US publication two years later that Epstein had no involvement in their company. Testimony shared with BBC Eye also raises questions about the role played by two other individuals who were active in the model industry, and whom the DOJ files show had close relationships with Epstein - former agent Ramsey Elkholy and agency director Faith Kates.

articles.title: Ukraine peace talks resume in Abu Dhabi after months-long pause
articles.summary: Kyiv, Washington and Moscow are all sending delegation to the United Arab Emirates for the first trilateral talks since February.
articles.body_text: Moscow and Kyiv are privately showing "a little bit of flexibility" on the issue of who would controls Ukraine's eastern regions in a postwar scenario, US officials have said. The comments came on the eve of the first trilateral talks aimed at ending the war in Ukraine since February. Senior officials from Moscow, Kyiv and Washington will meet in Abu Dhabi as the fifth anniversary of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine approaches. Jared Kushner - Donald Trump's son-in-law and part of the US delegation alongside peace envoy Steve Witkoff - said the talks would be focused on addressing the "postwar security concerns" of both Russia and Ukraine. "An important part of this process is encouraging all parties to begin thinking seriously about what comes after the war," Kushner wrote on X. But Moscow and Kyiv's positions on ending the conflict in the first place remain far apart. A key area of disagreement between the two involves Ukraine's eastern region of Donetsk, which is by now mostly occupied by Russia. Moscow has demanded that Ukraine relinquish the parts of Donetsk which it still holds, while Kyiv wants to freeze the contact line to maintain control over those sections, which it says are crucial to its future security. While neither side has budged on these demands, the US official speaking on the eve of the talks suggested that this was just the public stance and that Moscow and Kyiv had shown "a little bit of flexibility, privately". However, he acknowledged that the issue would not be solved without discussions about a new "security architecture". "They will not solve the Donetsk issue and the territorial issue until they know what the security architecture is going to be after the war," the official said. "And keep in mind, we're not going to be able to finalise one without the other." For Ukraine, a post-war "security architecture" may include reassurance that allies will come to its aid if it's attacked again. For Russia, that could be its longstanding ambition to see Nato roll back from eastern Europe – which would be alarming to Europeans.

articles.title: Trump says FBI investigating Nvidia boss's affair with alleged Chinese spy
articles.summary: The US president said he spoke with Jensen Huang on Monday and asked him about the affair with the alleged spy.
articles.body_text: Donald Trump has said the FBI is investigating the affair between the boss of Nvidia and an alleged Chinese spy. The US President said he spoke with chief executive Jensen Huang on Monday following reports that the US believed he had been targeted in a Chinese espionage campaign. "I asked him that question, 'Did you have any idea she was a spy?' He said 'I had no idea she was a spy' and I really believe him," Trump told reporters. Beijing has rejected claims that Huang was targeted, with its foreign ministry saying the allegations were "entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China". Nvidia, who has commissioned an independent investigation into the affair involving Alice Huang, alleged to be a Chinese spy, said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised. The revelations knocked about $250bn (£190bn) off the value of Nvidia during trading on Monday as the firm's share price fell by about 4%. Trump later told reporters at the White House that the FBI was now looking into the issue, but did not elaborate on the probe or when it was launched. The FBI declined to comment when contacted the BBC. US intelligence officials believe Alice Huang , also known as Huang Le, was a spy for Beijing, according to a New York Times report. The report said Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent a memo to top officials in Washington last spring warning that the Nvidia boss was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy. Alice Huang was managing director of Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has had dealings with Nvidia, the company at the centre at the development of AI worldwide through its microchips. Trump's remarks are the first indication of whether Huang knew about the woman's alleged ties to Chinese espionage. The American firm run, co-founded by Huang, is also a major focus in the AI rivalry between the US and China, with Washington officials treating the company's exports to Beijing as a matter of national security.

articles.title: Tyler Robinson: Trial date of alleged Charlie Kirk shooter set for June 2028
articles.summary: Tyler Robinson has pleaded not guilty to aggravated murder and six other charges in connection with the 2025 killing of the conservative activist.
articles.body_text: The trial of Tyler Robinson, the man accused of killing conservative activist Charlie Kirk, will start in June 2028, a judge has ordered. Robinson, 23, has pleaded not guilty to aggravated murder and six other charges in connection with the September 2025 killing of Kirk, 31, who was shot while he spoke at a Utah college campus. Utah County judge Tony Graf Jr on Monday told the court that jury selection would begin on 21 June, 2028. The prosecution has estimated the trial could last 17 weeks, while defence lawyers have said it could take seven months. Robinson could face the death penalty if found guilty of aggravated murder, something his defence team has sought to prevent. Prosecutors previously told the court they could be ready for trial by October 2027 but were willing to move that date back to January 2028 to avoid the holiday period. But defence attorneys said they needed more time to prepare their case and floated a 2029 start. As well as trying to stop Robinson facing the death penalty, they have also tried to have cameras banned from the courtroom. Kirk's widow, Erika, with whom he had two children, had pushed for as early a trial date as possible while also arguing proceedings should be live-streamed. She, along with Kirk's parents, ⁠Robert and Kathryn, have attended a number of court hearings in the case. At the end of Monday's proceedings, Erica Kirk's lawyer, Jeffrey A Nieman, told the judge that while "a trial in the summer of 2028, three years after Charlie's assassination, does not feel very speedy to the Kirk family", they had "no choice but obviously to accept the schedule the court's put forward". Nieman added: "The family has waited long enough already; they should not have to wait any longer for this." During a five-day preliminary hearing in July, prosecutors outlined their evidence to show probable cause for trial. This included DNA allegedly tying Robinson to the murder weapon and other items recovered at the scene; confessions he allegedly made to loved ones; and a taped video statement from his roommate and romantic partner, Lance Twiggs. "There is a mountain of evidence that proves that he is the shooter," prosecutor Ryan McBride told the court in September.

articles.title: Judge denies motion to dismiss Lindsay Clancy's murder case
articles.summary: The ruling means the case can move forward, possibly with reduced charges in a new trial.
articles.body_text: A Massachusetts judge has denied a motion to dismiss the murder case against Lindsay Clancy, the US woman accused of killing her three children. The judge's ruling follows her defence team's request to dismiss the case after the 12-person jury in her September trial failed to reach a verdict. Clancy has not denied killing her children in 2023, but her defence team argues she was suffering from severe postpartum psychosis at the time. Prosecutors say the killings were intentional. The ruling clears the way for prosecutors to pursue the case. They could reduce the charges in a potential second trial or dismiss them altogether. Clancy's defence team argued to dismiss the case against her due to double jeopardy - a legal standard that prevents a person from being tried for the same crime twice. Her lawyers argued that Judge William Sullivan, who presided over the 26-day jury trial last summer, acted prematurely when he declared a mistrial on 4 September, saying that he should have sought a viable alternative. The five-week trial, its lead-up and aftermath gripped Americans, and put postpartum mental health issues such as psychosis in the spotlight. In his ruling on Monday, Sullivan said that a retrial would not unconstitutionally subject Clancy to double jeopardy, according to court documents obtained by the BBC. The possibility that "an unreasonably stubborn or eccentric juror" could be seated is "an unavoidable risk of the jury system", he said. "Because the court concludes that there was manifest necessity for a mistrial based on the jury's deadlock, a retrial on the murder indictments does not violate Clancy's right not to be placed in double jeopardy." Sullivan also denied a defence motion to see records of the lone holdout juror in the case and to question the juror under oath. He said the defence failed to demonstrate that the records were needed for Clancy's defence at any retrial, and that questioning the juror "would have been impermissibly coercive".

articles.title: Republican Thomas Massie will force impeachment vote on Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth
articles.summary: The effort will likely fail, but Representative Thomas Massie wants to push Trump to fire Hegseth before Democrats can launch their own impeachment process next year.
articles.body_text: A Republican congressman plans to force a vote in the House of Representatives this week to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, alleging he has violated the US Constitution. "By engaging in hostilities in Iran for more than 90 days without congressional authorisation, Secretary Hegseth is breaking the law and must be held accountable," Representative Thomas Massie said. The effort will likely fail, as Republicans remain in power in Congress until January. But Massie says the effort is aimed at pushing President Donald Trump to replace Hegseth before Democrats can launch their own impeachment process. Hegseth has called the impeachment effort a "sham" and defended his record. "You see, they attack me. They attack us because we are effective," he said in a video statement last week. "It's not going to work. We will not back down." He called Massie a "disgruntled, defeated congressman" and said he was not concerned about the impeachment effort. In the video, Hegseth defended his leadership of the department and listed ways he has fulfilled Trump's America First agenda. Massie formally introduced his articles of impeachment in a resolution on the House floor on Monday afternoon. The move starts a 48-hour clock for the chamber to take up the measure. Lawmakers could vote on the resolution directly, vote to refer it to committee or to set it aside. "I'm doing this because it's the right thing to do," he told reporters after introducing the articles. Massie, who lost re-election earlier this year, has been critical of Trump and the war in Iran since it started nearly nine months ago. He has previously garnered headlines over demanding the Trump administration release the files related to deceased sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. The Kentucky congressman first introduced impeachment articles in September and has now brought them back in the wake of Republicans losing control of both the House and Senate in last week's midterm elections. He has said the effort was aimed at preventing a Democrat spectacle next year when they have control of Congress. He said he hoped to force Trump to name a replacement, who could be quickly confirmed while Republicans have power. "My effort to impeach Secretary Hegseth is a much gentler version of what's coming when the Democrats assume control of the House and Senate next year," Massie also said in a statement. "They will hold hearings and trials."

articles.title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

articles.body_text: Hundreds of billions of dollars have been wiped off the value of Nvidia after the US chipmaker announced an independent investigation would be carried out into its chief executive's affair with an alleged Chinese spy. The tech firm saw its shares fall by about 4% by close of trade on Monday after Jensen Huang admitted having an extramarital affair. Nvidia's probe came after reports that the US believed the Nvidia boss had been targeted in an espionage campaign by China. However, China has rejected the claims, with its foreign ministry saying allegations about Chinese spies were "entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China". Nvidia said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised, but a statement by the firm's board of directors said it would begin an investigation in "light of recent reporting that founder and chief executive Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort". US intelligence officials believe Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was a spy for Beijing, according to a New York Times report . The report said Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent a memo to top officials in Washington last spring warning that the Nvidia boss was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy. Alice Huang was managing director of Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has had dealings with Nvidia. Jensen Huang admitted he was "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children. He added he was "committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security" and would cooperate with the investigation. The Nvidia co-founder has also been requested to appear for a joint closed-door briefing for several Congressional committees next week. Members of the US House Foreign Affairs Committee last week asked Jensen Huang to appear for a closed-door briefing on his interactions with Alice Huang, as well as Nvidia's security protocols around espionage. "Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC's [China's] access to sensitive US technology and information," congressmen Brian Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford wrote in a letter.

articles.title: Turkey steel factory blast kills at least 17 people
articles.summary: Eyewitnesses say the explosion shook the ground, with one believing an earthquake had hit near the Habas Demir Celik plant in Aliaga.
articles.body_text: At least 17 people have died and 12 others have been injured in an explosion at an iron and steel factory near the port city of Izmir in western Turkey. All those killed and injured were workers at the Habas Demir Celik plant in Aliaga, one of the country's leading steel producers, authorities said. Footage from the scene showed a large fire inside the facility and a towering column of smoke rising into the air. The local governor said the blast happened around midday after a crane carrying a replacement boiler collapsed, causing materials to fall into a furnace below. Workplace accidents remain a chronic problem in Turkey, the Turkish Health and Safety Labor Watch, an independent civil society organisation, said. President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan originally said the death toll was 16, but the Health Minister, Kemal Memişoğlu, later announced that one of those who had been critically injured had later died, taking the toll to 17. Eyewitnesses at the scene said the explosion shook the ground, with one person initially believing an earthquake had struck. In a statement, the company that runs the factory said the accident occurred during scheduled maintenance work on one of the plant's electric arc furnaces. Izmir Governor Süleyman Elban told media that some people were believed to still be under the rubble. Speaking after a cabinet meeting on Monday, Erdoğan confirmed the deaths and said investigations were under way, while search and rescue operations continued. At least five people have been arrested, according BBC News's Turkish service, citing local media reports. The Habas plant is in the Izmir district of Aliaga which is a major port and one of Turkey's main shipbreaking hubs.

articles.title: France accuses Iran of supermarket fridge hacking
articles.summary: Tons of chilled and frozen food was spoiled last month as fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets heated up.
articles.body_text: France has accused Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) of being behind cyber-attacks that raised the temperatures of supermarket fridges and freezers across the country last month. Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said the attack was "unprecedented in both its scale and its level of aggression", adding those who were responsible would be hit with sanctions. Iran has yet to respond officially, but some Iranian media outlets have dismissed the allegations as baseless. The French hacking, which led to the destruction of tons of frozen and chilled food in France was followed by a similar attack against supermarkets across several other European countries. It is not known if the instances are linked. Barrot said the attack on France's supermarkets "marks the first large-scale cyber-attack aimed at sabotage on our national territory, and it constitutes a major attack on the nation's interests and the security of the French people". He said the government had summoned the Iranian ambassador to Paris to "lodge a very strong protest against this extremely grave act". France will take "any other necessary and proportionate measures" to respond to the incident and "deter anyone who might seek to repeat it", Barrot added. The Paris prosecutor said an investigation had been opened into the head of an offensive cyber unit associated with the IRGC as well as his two deputies. Laure Beccuau named the unit as Shahid Kaveh, which she said had an affiliation with the electronic and cyber centre of the IRGC. Shahid Kaveh is the name given to a cluster of hackers thought to be directly employed by the Iranian regime. In recent weeks, a number of commentators and politicians in Iran have argued that the country should extend any retaliation beyond the Middle East if the US and Israel resume the war they started earlier this year. If the IRGC carried out the cyber-attacks, it remains unclear whether they were part of Iran's deterrence strategy.

articles.title: Trump questions elections integrity after previously accepting midterm results
articles.summary: Trump made the claims, without evidence, on Truth Social on Monday.
articles.body_text: US President Donald Trump has questioned the legitimacy of the midterm election results in which Republicans suffered sweeping losses, days after saying he would accept the outcome. "Does anybody really believe that this 'Election' was honest. How could the Polls be so wrong?" Trump wrote on Truth Social on Monday. This appeared to contradict what he told the New York Times on election night that he was "absolutely willing" to accept the results. Democrats retook both chambers of Congress in last week's elections. State and local officials across the US said voting had been mostly problem-free. Some key races, including Senate contests in Alaska and Mississippi, have yet to be called. In the Truth Social post, Trump made vague claims about polling, voting "dumps", and "machines" without providing specific evidence of what this referred to and whether he believed there had been error or wrongdoing. The reporting of vote counts on election night proceeded as normal, according to Charles Stewart III, a political scientist at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). "We saw across the nation the standard patterns we see in terms of when the votes are reported," he said. Stewart added that in some states, like Florida and Georgia, some initial reporting of results happens quickly because they already have the results of early and mail ballots. Trump has previously attempted to cast doubts on the integrity of elections he has lost, although he himself was not on the ballot in the midterms. "We would have won easily if I was on the ballot," Trump told CBS News, the BBC's US partner, after it was confirmed his party had lost both the Senate and the House. Surveys ahead of the election from several pollsters and news outlets suggested that Republicans could lose seats in both the House and Senate.

articles.title: Russia-Ukraine war: Nine Zimbabweans caught trying to leave South Africa to join conflict
articles.summary: Hundreds of people from different African countries have been recruited to fight for Russia, according to Ukraine.
articles.body_text: Nine Zimbabweans have been arrested in South Africa after they were caught allegedly trying to leave the country to fight in the war between Russia and the Ukraine, police say. The group, aged between 20 and 26, were arrested in and around Johannesburg by a multidisciplinary team on Sunday evening. They were caught as they were "preparing to board flights out of the country", authorities added, but their final destination is unclear. They have been charged with contravening South Africa's Regulation of Foreign Military Assistance Act, which outlaws mercenary activity without government permission. Police said five people were arrested at South Africa's biggest airport, OR Tambo, and another four at a hotel in Bruma, east of Johannesburg by a multidisciplinary team that involved Interpol. All nine later appeared in court, according to state prosecutors. The police statement added that the involvement of Interpol and other international law enforcement agencies indicated that the suspects had also allegedly violated laws in their respective home countries, prompting cooperation with South African authorities. They have also not said whether the group allegedly intended to fight for Russia or Ukraine nor provided details of the organisations allegedly involved in facilitating their travel. Citizens of several African countries, including Kenya, Ghana and South Africa, have gone to fight for Russia in Ukraine - some they had been duped and had not realised where they were going. A Ukrainian intelligence assessment estimated earlier this year that more than 1,700 people from 36 countries in Africa have been recruited to fight for Russia. Kenya at the time estimated that 252 citizens had been illegally conscripted in Russia. In March, Foreign Minister Musalia Mudavadi visited Moscow to address the issue. He said at the time that an agreement had been reached to stop recruiting Kenyan nationals.

articles.body_text: Samahara Lobatón y Renato Rossini Jr. se encuentran en el ojo público luego de sorprender a sus seguidores al anunciar su romance. De hecho, la relación se habría fortalecido durante su participación en el reality “El Sultanato”, donde surgieron los primeros rumores de un posible vínculo sentimental. Sin embargo, semanas después, la hija de Melissa Klug confirmó su relación mediante una emotiva publicación en redes sociales. La noticia generó diversas reacciones entre sus seguidores: mientras algunos cuestionaron el romance, otros se interesaron por el futuro de la pareja y se preguntaron si ambos tenían planes de tener un hijo. En la siguiente nota te contamos todo lo que debes saber al respecto. Mientras Samahara Lobatón y Renato Rossini Jr. disfrutan de su romance tras confirmar su relación, sus seguidores han mostrado curiosidad por conocer los planes a futuro de la pareja. En ese contexto, una internauta le preguntó a la influencer, durante una dinámica en Instagram, si deseaba tener un bebé con el modelo. Ante la consulta, la hija de Melissa Klug respondió en sus historias que no tiene entre sus planes volver a convertirse en madre debido a que se sometió a una ligadura de trompas. Aunque dejó abierta la posibilidad de que en el futuro la decisión pueda cambiar y traer al mundo a su cuarto hijo. En tanto, la creadora de contenidos dejó en claro que ahora se encuentra enfocada en sus planes profesionales. “Desde lo más bonito les responderé a todos, ¡yo estoy ligada! No está en mis planes tener más bebés, quiero seguir creciendo en lo que me gusta y sobre todo seguir trabajando. Ahora, no descarto que de acá a 10 o 15 años esto vaya a cambiar, pero por el momento no”, escribió Lobatón. En una entrevista para el podcast de Magaly Medina, Samahara Lobatón se presentó para hablar acerca de su faceta como madre y sus desafíos laborales tanto en la televisión como en las plataformas digitales. Sin embargo, no dejó de destacar el importante papel que cumplen sus nanas, quienes se encargan del cuidado de sus pequeños hijos mientras ella permanece enfocada en sus proyectos profesionales. Asimismo, señaló que asume los principales gastos de sus hijos, además de cubrir las necesidades esenciales del hogar. Frente a ello, la popular ‘Urraca’ le consultó cómo afronta estas responsabilidades económicas y si los realities en los que participó le permitieron obtener los ingresos necesarios para mantener una vida estable. Esto llevó a que la joven influencer expresara su agradecimiento por el buen momento laboral que atraviesa; aunque dejó entrever que la remuneración que recibió por participar en ‘La granja VIP’ estuvo por debajo de sus expectativas. “No me puedo quejar, Dios está conmigo pese a todo. Sí, pero el de ‘La Granja’ no puedo decir mucho, pero no fue gran cosa”, contó.

articles.title: Feriados noviembre 2026 en Perú: ¿Cuántos feriados y días no laborables tiene?
articles.summary: El calendario peruano de 2026 contempla fechas especiales durante noviembre. Conoce cuántos feriados quedan este mes, qué días se celebran y si habrá jornadas de descanso para los trabajadores del sector público y privado.
articles.body_text: Los días libres son una oportunidad para compartir tiempo en familia, organizar actividades personales o realizar pequeños viajes sin las obligaciones habituales del trabajo. En noviembre de 2026, el calendario peruano contempla fechas de descanso que deben distinguirse entre feriados nacionales y días no laborables establecidos de manera extraordinaria. Estas últimas disposiciones están vinculadas con la visita del papa León XIV al Perú y comprenden jornadas y horarios específicos en Lima, Callao y otras regiones del país. Además, no todos los trabajadores tendrán las mismas condiciones para acceder a estos descansos, pues algunas medidas requieren compensar posteriormente las horas que se dejen de trabajar. Conoce qué fechas están previstas para noviembre, en qué lugares se aplicarán y cuáles son las diferencias que debes tener en cuenta antes de organizar tus actividades. El calendario de noviembre tiene un feriado nacional, el pasado 1 de noviembre, día de todos los santos, sin embargo; también cuenta con días NO laborables según lo indica la ley. Estas últimas fueron oficializadas mediante el Decreto Supremo N.º 020-2026-TR, publicado en el diario oficial El Peruano. El calendario contempla las siguientes fechas: La compensación dependerá del sector laboral. En las entidades públicas, las horas pendientes deberán recuperarse dentro de los diez días posteriores al descanso o cuando lo determine el titular de cada institución, de acuerdo con las necesidades del servicio. En las empresas privadas, empleadores y trabajadores podrán acordar cómo reponer el tiempo no trabajado. Si no consiguen llegar a un consenso, el empleador establecerá las condiciones para realizar la compensación correspondiente. Aunque ambas fechas permiten interrumpir las actividades habituales, tienen condiciones distintas. El feriado constituye un descanso obligatorio reconocido por ley y no requiere recuperar las horas que correspondían a esa jornada. En cambio, los días no laborables suelen estar dirigidos principalmente al sector público y contemplan la recuperación posterior del tiempo pendiente. Para los trabajadores privados, su aplicación depende del acuerdo entre empleadores y trabajadores. Según la Cámara de Comercio de Lima (CCL), si un empleado trabaja en un día feriado debido a necesidades de la empresa o rotación de turnos, y no recibe un día libre en sustitución, debe recibir una compensación económica equivalente a tres veces su salario habitual por esa jornada laboral. Esto se debe a tres conceptos: No cumplir con el pago adicional o negar la compensación de descanso constituye una infracción muy grave en materia laboral. Las sanciones económicas varían según el tipo de empresa, y pueden ir desde poco más de 1.000 soles hasta superar los 24.000.

Además, no todos los trabajadores tendrán las mismas condiciones para acceder a estos descansos, pues algunas medidas requieren compensar posteriormente las horas que se dejen de trabajar. Conoce qué fechas están previstas para noviembre, en qué lugares se aplicarán y cuáles son las diferencias que debes tener en cuenta antes de organizar tus actividades. El calendario de noviembre tiene un feriado nacional, el pasado 1 de noviembre, día de todos los santos, sin embargo; también cuenta con días NO laborables según lo indica la ley. En las entidades públicas, las horas pendientes deberán recuperarse dentro de los diez días posteriores al descanso o cuando lo determine el titular de cada institución, de acuerdo con las necesidades del servicio. En las empresas privadas, empleadores y trabajadores podrán acordar cómo reponer el tiempo no trabajado. articles.body_text: El precio del dólar inició la jornada de este lunes con una referencia de S/3,420 en el mercado cambiario peruano, por debajo de los S/3,426 del cierre anterior. La moneda estadounidense perdió terreno frente al sol, en línea con el debilitamiento del dólar a nivel internacional, cuyo índice DXY retrocedió 0,44%, hasta los 101.8 puntos. La apertura estuvo marcada por la caída de los precios del petróleo y la recuperación de los metales, mientras los inversionistas esperan nuevos datos de inflación en Estados Unidos. “Los mercados estarán atentos a la publicación de la inflación estadounidense, prevista para este martes 10 de noviembre, luego de conocerse cifras de empleo superiores a las expectativas en octubre. Estos resultados serán importantes para evaluar las próximas decisiones de tasas de interés de la Reserva Federal y su impacto sobre el dólar y las monedas emergentes”, explicó Jorge Luis Huayta, trader FX de Kambista. En los mercados internacionales, el petróleo Brent retrocedió 4,39% y el WTI cayó 3,33%, ante reportes sobre una posible reducción de las tensiones en el estrecho de Ormuz. En contraste, la plata avanzó 1,54%, el oro subió 1,31% y el cobre ganó 1,28%. Este comportamiento se produjo mientras la inflación al productor en China alcanzó el 5.7% interanual en octubre, su nivel más alto en más de cuatro años, generando nuevas expectativas sobre los costos de los insumos industriales. En el ámbito local, la atención estará centrada en la decisión de política monetaria del Banco Central de Reserva (BCR), prevista para el jueves 12 de noviembre. Asimismo, el Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI) proyecta que el PBI peruano alcanzaría los US$413.597 millones en 2027, ligeramente por encima de los US$413.443 millones estimados para Chile. De cara a los próximos días, el análisis de Kambista señala que la publicación de la inflación estadounidense y la decisión de tasas del BCR serán los principales factores de seguimiento para el mercado cambiario. También se conocerán las cifras de la balanza comercial peruana de septiembre, previstas para el miércoles 11 de noviembre, mientras la evolución del cobre, los precios del petróleo y las tensiones geopolíticas podrían generar nuevos movimientos en la cotización del dólar frente al sol.

articles.title: Un 93,1 % de los clientes de Ueno bank han recibido devoluciones de ahorros en Paraguay

articles.body_text: Un 93,1 % de los clientes en Paraguay de Ueno bank, la entidad intervenida por problemas de solvencia, han recibido hasta este lunes devoluciones de ahorros, informó el Banco Central, al estar cobijados por un mecanismo estatal de garantía. En total, detalló la entidad emisora, se trata de 1.738.804 de cuentas cubiertas por el Fondo de Garantía de Depósitos con un desembolso global que asciende a 2,126 billones de guaraníes (unos 340,4 millones de dólares). Previamente se estimaba una cifra de 2,9 millones de clientes, pero fueron descartadas del total aquellas cuentas sin saldos a favor, duplicadas y con deudas, entre otras. La institución emisora ha explicado que la primera tanda de desembolsos ya ha cubierto al total de ahorristas con montos acumulados desde uno hasta 10 millones de guaraníes (unos 1.601,32 dólares). El segundo desembolso ha sido para cuentas con saldos intermedios, de los 10 millones de guaraníes a 40 salarios mínimos, que equivalen a 121,7 millones de guaraníes (unos 20.353 dólares al cambio actual). A este grupo se le ha aplicado el descuento de los préstamos que el cliente tuviera pendientes con Ueno bank. El Banco Central de Paraguay tiene como límite legal cubrir cuentas hasta 75 salarios mínimos (228,3 millones de guaraníes / 38.622 dólares aproximadamente), por lo que todavía está pendiente de abonar la diferencia desde los 40 salarios mínimos hasta los 75. Los clientes recibirán en los próximos días la diferencia pendiente. Los que superen el límite de cobertura del Fondo de Garantía (fondos, inversiones, grandes empresas, recursos estatales o pensiones) no se ha precisado todavía que ocurrirá. Empresas estatales habían trasladado a Ueno bank 800 millones de dólares, gran parte de ellos recursos pensionales. La semana pasada, el Banco Central anunció el comienzo del proceso de intervención de Ueno bank, que prevé la activación de los mecanismos del Fondo de Garantía. El miércoles pasado, un día después de la intervención de Ueno, Peña, quien todavía ejercía la presidencia, promulgó una ley aprobada en tiempo récord por el Congreso para agilizar la entrega, en un plazo mínimo de 24 horas, de los recursos retenidos a miles de clientes. El periodo para el pago de ese anticipo vence este miércoles 11 de noviembre, detalló hoy el BCP.

articles.title: Piura: Senamhi advierte altas temperaturas de hasta 36°C y no descarta lluvias
articles.summary: La entidad meteorológica informó que el aumento de la temperatura estará vigente desde este lunes 9 hasta el jueves 12 de noviembre.
articles.body_text: El Servicio Nacional de Meteorología e Hidrología del Perú (Senamhi) advirtió sobre el incremento de las temperaturas en la costa norte, donde los valores podrían superar los 36 °C durante los próximos días. La alerta meteorológica estará vigente desde este lunes 9 hasta el jueves 12 de noviembre. La Dirección Zonal 1 del Senamhi precisó que el incremento de la temperatura estará acompañado de una mayor radiación ultravioleta y ráfagas de viento que podrían alcanzar velocidades cercanas a los 45 kilómetros por hora. De acuerdo con el Aviso Meteorológico Regional N.° 206 de Senamhi, las temperaturas máximas en la costa norte oscilarán entre los 23 °C y 36 °C, mientras que en la sierra norte se esperan registros de entre 19 °C y 32 °C. El pronóstico contempla tres niveles de intensidad: amarillo, por condiciones moderadas; naranja, por intensidad fuerte; y rojo, por condiciones extremas. Asimismo, la institución meteorológica señaló que no se descartan lluvias en la costa norte. La posibilidad de precipitaciones responde a las condiciones atmosféricas que se vienen registrando en la región. En otro reporte, Senamhi informó que Piura registró importantes acumulados de lluvia durante la semana pasada. La localidad de Alamor presentó el mayor registro, con 35,8 milímetros, seguido de Hacienda Barrios (18,1 mm), Partidor (13.8 mm), Paimas (10.5 mm) y El Ciruelo (7.4 mm). La entidad también reportó que el contenido de agua precipitable (PWAT) en Piura supera los 55 milímetros y alcanza valores cercanos a los 62 milímetros. Este indicador evidencia una concentración de humedad en la atmósfera, condición que puede favorecer la formación de precipitaciones cuando coincide con escenarios de inestabilidad atmosférica y ascenso del aire. Ante este panorama, se recomienda a los ciudadanos de Piura y otras localidades de la costa norte mantenerse atentos a los comunicados oficiales del Senamhi.

articles.title: Hotel giant Wyndham exposed customer data after app security lapse | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Exclusive: Wyndham left a hardcoded credential in its customer app, allowing anyone to access customer data. The hotel giant wouldn't say if it has the ability to check for any past unauthorized access.
articles.body_text: Hotel and resort giant Wyndham has acknowledged a cybersecurity incident after a good-faith security researcher discovered a bug that allowed anyone to access customers’ personal information. Security researcher Robert Wiggins at What Security exclusively told TechCrunch that he found a password inside the source code of Wyndham’s Android app, which granted access to an internal company database, hosted by tech company Salesforce. Wiggins told TechCrunch that the credential exposed personal information including customer names, email addresses, and Wyndham member number. The database also stores customer login tokens ( called JWTs ) that keep customers logged-in to their apps without having to repeatedly enter their own passwords. The database also contained Wyndham files and documents. According to Wiggins, the database had millions of entries, but he was unable to determine an accurate number of exposed customer records. Wyndham touts some 129 million enrolled rewards members. The researcher said Wyndham has no way to report security flaws, and asked for TechCrunch’s help in alerting the company. Soon after TechCrunch made contact with Wyndham’s cybersecurity staff, the exposed credential was revoked, preventing any further access to the database. “Our team has taken steps to address the issue,” a Wyndham spokesperson told TechCrunch. “Our security teams have no evidence of any unauthorized access,” the statement added, without providing any further details about the claim. Wyndham’s spokesperson would not say, when asked, whether the company had the technical means, such as server logs, to determine if anyone had access to the customer database prior to Wiggins’ discovery. TechCrunch also asked Wyndham whether it planned to notify customers whose information was exposed, or disclose the incident to U.S. regulators, such as filing notice with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, as public companies are required to do for material cybersecurity incidents. Wyndham would not say. Wyndham’s spokesperson also would not say for how long the password was embedded in its customer app, or how Wyndham plans to ship a long-term fix for the app. App and software developers generally avoid including passwords or credentials in publicly released software and apps — a process known as “hardcoding” — as anyone with a copy of the software can extract the password and use it to access its associated server or database. Given the simplicity with which credentials can be abused by anyone, many cases of hardcoded credentials are automatically scored with a maximum vulnerability severity rating. For Wiggins, this is his second public discovery of hardcoded credentials in two weeks, after finding a near-identical vulnerability in Applebee’s app that exposed customer data. Wiggins relied on AI tools for both discoveries, which make it easier to identify simple security weaknesses, such as hardcoded credentials, by scouring thousands of lines of decompiled app code every second. When asked about Wyndham’s response, Wiggins told TechCrunch that he was glad the company fixed the issue, but noted that without visibility into any past activity, someone with malicious intent could have leaked large amounts of customers’ personal information.

U.S. intelligence officials believe she was recruited by the Chinese government to collect intelligence on Jensen Huang and influence his position regarding U.S. export controls on advanced AI chips. articles.title: The race is on to sue Nvidia | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Nvidia’s stock slid more than 4% after its board opened an investigation into Jensen Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, and one securities law expert says the company’s earlier insistence that it was all “normal” could turn into a very expensive problem.
articles.body_text: Nvidia’s stock slid more than 4% on Monday, the first trading day after its board said it would investigate CEO Jensen Huang over his relationship with Alice Huang, an executive U.S. intelligence believes was spying for China. Securities lawyers were already moving. Several firms, including Schall, Brown & Schwartz, Levi & Korsinsky, Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman, and The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz, announced investigations Monday into whether Nvidia made false or misleading statements or failed to disclose information that’s pertinent to investors. Robert Bartlett, a Stanford Law professor and securities law expert, expects them to have plenty of company. “I would definitely wager that there’ll be a filing,” Bartlett said in an interview Monday morning, adding that he wouldn’t be surprised if a case had been filed by the end of day. Plaintiffs’ lawyers have good reasons to be first in line; under federal securities law, the first complaint triggers a public notice, and investors then have 60 days to ask the court to be named lead plaintiff. A firm that files early gets a head start on signing up investors with large losses, as well as on shaping the story of the case. Nvidia is headquartered in Santa Clara, and indeed, that’s where one of the first cases surfaced Monday afternoon. Rosen Law Firm, a New York-based plaintiffs’ firm that specializes in securities class actions, filed the case Monday in federal court in the Northern District of California. (The firm was lead counsel in a $250 million settlement with Alibaba and ranks among the most active filers of such cases.) The suit was brought on behalf of Mark Kistenmacher, who’s described as an individual investor. According to the complaint, Kistenmacher made seven purchases totaling roughly $20,500 between February and November of this year. The proposed class covers anyone who bought Nvidia securities between Oct. 9, 2025, and Nov. 8, 2026, and the suit names both Nvidia and Huang. The complaint accuses them of misleading investors about Huang’s ties to Megaspeed, the Singapore-based data center outfit where Alice Huang was considered a top executive. It points to three statements: Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo’s claim that Huang’s interactions with Alice Huang were “not unusual or unexpected,” the company’s claim that it found “ no evidence of diversion ” of its chips, and Jensen Huang’s Oct. 30 comment to Bloomberg that Nvidia’s dealings with Megaspeed were “ normal and not unusual .” All three were false or misleading, the suit says, because Huang was having an affair with Alice Huang. Kistenmacher is asking for unspecified damages, interest and attorneys’ fees, and he wants a jury trial. While much remains unknown, the legal theory here doesn’t depend on anything the board’s investigation turns up about Huang’s private life. When The New York Times first reported on Huang’s ties to Alice Huang last month, Rizzo really did tell the Times that the relationship was “ not unusual or unexpected .” Rizzo separately told another outlet , The Hill, that “Megaspeed has been no different than many other regional cloud customers. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year.” Since then, Huang has acknowledged to the board that the relationship was intimate. Meanwhile, The Times reports that U.S. intelligence had been monitoring Alice Huang for more than a year. From a securities perspective, Bartlett said, the company’s earlier statement was “clearly a misleading statement.” And because Huang is CEO, Bartlett said, “his knowledge gets imputed to the company.” In other words, Nvidia is treated as having known what its chief executive knew. The Kistenmacher complaint makes the same argument. Bartlett says the likely vehicle is a “classic fraud on the market” claim, in which investors argue they paid prices that reflected false or incomplete public information, and lost money when the truth emerged. This early lawsuit relies on that theory, and Monday’s drop of $7.97 per share, or 4.27%, gives the attorneys involved a lot to work with. Damages in such cases are tied to the stock’s decline, and Nvidia is one of the most valuable companies in the world, so you can imagine a settlement could prove exceedingly expensive. The usual path is that the case is litigated for a long time and then settles, Bartlett notes. That means a large payment from the company and its directors-and-officers insurers, but typically no personal consequences for the CEO or the board. It is also a civil matter, so Huang isn’t facing prison over it. The irony, as Bartlett noted, is that the suit is brought in the name of Nvidia’s shareholders, and shareholders ultimately pay for the settlement, directly or through insurance premiums.

articles.title: Anthropic releases new Mythos and Fable models amid RSI concerns | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Anthropic says the new models "show improvements in areas like coding, reasoning, and vision," as well as in communicating more clearly with users.
articles.body_text: Anthropic released new versions of its most advanced models on Monday, with the launch of Mythos 5.2 and Fable 5.2. The company says the new models “show improvements in areas like coding, reasoning, and vision” and communicate more clearly with users. Notably, Anthropic is lowering the cost of Fable from $10 to $8 per million input tokens. As a result, Fable 5.2 is now cheaper than its primary competitor GPT-6 Astra. Anthropic says that the new version of Fable will return responses 30% faster across effort levels. Faster inference serving is available for double the price. Fable 5.2 is also compatible with zero data retention (ZDR) policies through the Enterprise Frontier Safeguards system , long a sticking point for many enterprise clients. It’s Anthropic’s first model release since the arrival of a third-party report from the assessment group METR , which suggested the lab might be approaching recursive self-improvement (RSI) — or the ability for AI models to carry on model training independently. The METR report found internal models were speeding up Anthropic’s AI progress by roughly 2x, although many uncertainties remain. Still, Anthropic’s release notes significant ongoing challenges in accurately testing model capabilities. “Claude Mythos 5.2 and Fable 5.2 each voice suspicion that they are being evaluated more often than any of our recent models, which challenges our ability to assess how they will act in real-world settings. As these settings expand and capabilities increase with future models, we expect this challenge to grow.” Anthropic maintains that the new version of Mythos does not have the ability to act covertly against its user, a verdict that’s detailed further in Mythos 5.2’s system card . “Claude Mythos 5.2 shows stronger covert capabilities than prior Claude models on several of our evaluations, particularly when its reasoning is hidden from the monitor,” the system card reads. “That said, we believe that low levels of absolute performance on our new covert evaluations support claims that rely on detection of harmful actions in high-stakes situations.” Fable 5.2 has been available to select parties in pre-release for some time, and Anthropic says the model has already “solved two open problems in theoretical physics, formalized Fermat’s Last Theorem, and supported numerous other research projects.” Also on Monday, AI startup Physical Superintelligence announced a new proof of the Aaronson‑Ambainis conjecture, a pivotal step in setting theoretical limits for quantum computing. Notably, the lab said the result was achieved by running “a non-public Anthropic model” within PSI’s own system. Anthropic did not confirm or deny whether Fable 5.2 was the model in question. Jensen Huang admitted to the affair and apologized in a memo to the company on Sunday. U.S. intelligence officials believe Alice Huang was recruited by Chinese intelligence to gather information about the CEO and influence the company’s efforts to loosen chip export restrictions. Nvidia’s independent directors, working with outside legal counsel, are investigating the matter, and Congress is already demanding answers . The controversy comes at a sensitive moment for Nvidia. Historically, China has been a big market for the company. It has shrunk in recent years due to strict U.S. export controls and an aggressive push by Beijing for domestic alternatives. In the three months ended July 26, Nvidia recorded $7.9 billion in revenue from customers headquartered in China, roughly 8% of total revenue. Huang has repeatedly lobbied the U.S. government to expand access to China , and some of his persuasion tactics have been successful. Huang met repeatedly with President Donald Trump and administration officials last year; afterward, the government reversed restrictions on Nvidia’s H20 chips and allowed exports of its more powerful H200 processors. On numerous occasions, Huang has publicly lamented export controls, calling them a “ failure ” at a conference last year and saying in May that it was “ not wise ” for the U.S. and China to create two distinct AI ecosystems. He has also warned that shutting Nvidia out of China’s compute market would enable the country to develop its own AI chips to challenge Nvidia internationally. China is already moving in that direction. Reuters reported last week that about 600,000 H200 chips are being held in Hong Kong, awaiting shipment to mainland China. Beijing is pushing AI companies to prioritize buying chips from Chinese companies instead. The idea that Huang needed any encouragement in the form of an attractive woman to push for greater access to China seems like a stretch, particularly because his lobbying efforts predate their reported meeting at an Nvidia event in early 2024. At the end of the day, Huang is a salesman trying to dominate one of the world’s biggest AI markets. Still, the allegations involving Alice Huang open new scrutiny of the company’s business relationships and could taint any assurances Nvidia offers that it can prevent sensitive technology from reaching unauthorized customers. Once made, rumors of questionable allegiances can be hard to shake. Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly warned officials close to Trump earlier this year about Huang’s relationship with an alleged spy. Even if Nvidia’s investigation finds that Huang didn’t share secrets with his paramour, the question is whether he’ll be able to convince Washington that Nvidia can still responsibly do business with China. articles.title: Anthropic joins AI’s natural gas frenzy, buys $3.4B worth of turbines | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Anthropic bought billions of dollars' worth of natural gas turbines in a deal that could give it buyer's remorse.
articles.body_text: AI’s power crunch has become so acute that Anthropic, a company that has generally avoided buying physical infrastructure, is spending $3.4 billion on natural gas turbines. The AI company, which is planning to go public this year, is buying Caterpillar generators that equipment supplier OnePWR had originally ordered, according to a Financial Times report . The generators are capable of producing up to 1.7 gigawatts of electricity. Historically, Anthropic has preferred to rent rather than buy. The company disclosed in its S-1 filing in May that it is paying SpaceX subsidiary xAI $1.25 billion per month through May 2029 to use xAI’s computing power. “We expect to enter into additional similar services contracts,” Anthropic stated in the filing, meaning more deals to rent computing power. But as demand for compute ramps up, the market for power has also grown increasingly uncertain, which may have forced its hand. The backlog for natural gas turbines stretches into the early 2030s, and queues to connect to the electrical grid can be just as long. Anthropic’s purchase looks like a last resort. According to the report, OnePWR ordered the turbines a couple years ago but couldn’t find financing to complete the purchase. Anthropic had planned to buy them from OnePWR but instead went directly to Caterpillar, the manufacturer. It’s not clear why OnePWR was unable to secure financing despite Anthropic’s apparent interest as a customer. Whatever the case, Anthropic likely wanted to keep the generating capacity to itself rather than give a competitor an opportunity to snap it up. AI companies have been ramping up their purchases of natural gas equipment and supplies in recent years. Google , Amazon , Microsoft , and Meta have all announced plans to build massive natural gas power plants to power their data centers on-site, rather than drawing from the public grid. The binge has given a second wind to fracking , the drilling method used to extract natural gas from underground rock. And if the buildout proceeds as planned, U.S. data centers alone could consume more natural gas than Germany and Japan combined by 2035. The reliance on natural gas also exposes hyperscalers to price fluctuations. One analyst expects that prices could more than triple by the end of the decade in some markets. If that happens, Anthropic might have a serious case of buyer’s remorse. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: Waymo robotaxis kept illegally passing school buses after software fix, feds say | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The update to Waymo's self-driving system was rolled out nearly a year ago.
articles.body_text: Nearly a year ago, Waymo updated its self-driving software and issued a recall after numerous reports that its robotaxis were illegally passing school buses that had stopped and deployed flashing red lights. Now, federal safety regulators have opened a new investigation into why that behavior has continued. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) said in a November 6 filing that a majority of these reported incidents occurred after the company deployed a software update intended to fix the problem. Reuters was the first to report the filing. Waymo said last year that a software update was completed for all affected vehicles on November 17, 2025. However, NHTSA said the majority of the incidents occurred after the software update. NHTSA’s Office of Defects Investigation (ODI) has opened a “recall query” to “assess the adequacy of the remedy.” The ODI opened its initial investigation into Waymo in October 2025 after seeing footage of one of its autonomous vehicles maneuvering around a stopped school bus that had its stop sign extended, lights flashing, and was unloading children in Atlanta. In that incident, a Waymo robotaxi crossed perpendicularly in front of the school bus from its right side. The autonomous vehicle then turned left around the front of the bus before traveling down the street. Numerous other incidents have been documented in the weeks and months since in Austin, where Waymo also operates a robotaxi service. Austin Independent School District officials reported at least five such incidents at the time, according to a letter filed with NHTSA. Reached for comment, Waymo stressed the importance of safety to its mission. “We have made significant improvements to vehicle behavior around school buses and have received no citations since March 2026,” a spokesperson told TechCrunch via email. “The Waymo Driver has a clearly demonstrated positive impact on roadway safety. Once received, we’ll work to respond to NHTSA’s query and look forward to continuing our engagement on recall processes for AV software that continues to learn and improve.” TechCrunch also reached out to Austin Independent School District officials for comment and will update the article if they respond. articles.title: Musk says Tesla will refund some Cybertruck deposits, defends decision to end production | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Elon Musk defended the company's decision to stop making the Cybertruck, which will go out of production in around eight months.
articles.body_text: Tesla CEO Elon Musk is defending the Cybertruck and the company’s decision to stop producing the polarizing steel-clad truck, claiming that the order rate far exceeds its production. Tesla will shut down production of the Cybertruck in about eight months Musk said in an X post on Monday. He also said the company will try to make as many of the vehicles as possible before then, though Tesla will “have to return deposits for a lot of people.” Musk argued the Cybertruck was not unprofitable, and that Tesla was ending production because the “opportunity cost of the complexity of Cybertruck is vastly outweighed by the value of incremental Cybercab production.” In other words, Musk is arguing that Tesla can make more money by using the factory space and resources dedicated to the Cybertruck for building Cybercab robotaxis. Musk said last week that Tesla plans to use the factory space to build more two-seater Cybercabs. The first Cybertrucks were delivered to customers in late 2023, when it seemed like it could be a breakthrough hit for the company. Reservations for the vehicle had ballooned to 1 million, according to Musk , who also predicted that the company would sell around 250,000 of the trucks annually. But those reservations never translated into actual sales. Tesla doesn’t break out sales of the Cybertrucks, but industry experts estimate a total of about 71,000 Cybertrucks have been sold since the first deliveries began in November 2023. Many of those sales came from inside Musk’s ecosystem of other businesses. For instance, SpaceX (now known as SpaceXSI), which he also leads and is the largest shareholder of, purchased $131 million worth of Cybertrucks from Tesla in 2025, according to the company’s S-1 registration statement ahead of its IPO. Another Musk company, xAI, also bought $430 million worth of Tesla Megapacks for its data centers, before it merged with SpaceX. But sales of the Cybertruck, which lagged for months, could see a final bump now that it’s going out of production. Still, even a scarcity boost is unlikely to push the truck’s demand to the lofty projections from several years ago. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission .
